chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abu al-Bilad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

A Bedouin came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'Teach me a deed by which I may enter Paradise.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Feed people and spread the greeting of peace.' The Bedouin said, 'I cannot endure that.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do you have camels?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'So look after a camel and provide water for it for a family who do not drink water except intermittently, so that perhaps your camel will not be exhausted and your water-skin will not be damaged until Paradise becomes obligatory for you.'
ai.seo_question: What practical deed did the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) suggest for someone who found general acts of worship too difficult?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him) tailors spiritual guidance to the Bedouin’s capacity, offering a manageable act of charity—providing water to a family intermittently while caring for a camel—as a sustainable path to Paradise. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on gradualism (tadrij) and the practicality of worship, where consistent, small deeds are valued over overwhelming, short-lived efforts. The narrative underscores the importance of animal welfare and communal care as integral components of faith.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Yahya Bin Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad, from his father, from his grandfather, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A Bedouin came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘Teach me a deed by which I can enter the Paradise’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Feed the food, and initiate the greeting’. So he said, ‘I cannot endure that’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So is there a camel for you?’ He said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So prepare a camel and usher to it a family who are not drinking the water except for intermittently. Thus, they would neither exhaust your camel nor would they damage your water container, until the Paradise is Obligated for you’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad from his father from his grandfather who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once an Arab man came to the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘Teach me a good deed whereby I can go to Paradise . 5

He (the Holy Prophet) said, ‘Serve food and offer greetings of peace aloud . 5 He (the Imam) has said that the man then said, ‘I cannot afford this . 5 He (the Holy Prophet) asked, ‘Do you have a camel ? 5 The man replied, ‘Yes, I have a camel . 5 He (the Holy Prophet) then said, ‘Prepare your camel and provide water for a family who need water only every other day. This will not destroy your camel or damage your water container before your going to Paradise becomes necessary. ‘“
